# Service Menu Build — For Grace

• **Start with your revenue reality, not your dreams.** Pull last month's transactions: which services actually generate income? Which sit empty? Build your menu around what sells NOW, then add aspirational offerings. Don't list 12 things if 3 drive 80% of revenue.

• **Split into two documents immediately.** Coaches need *delivery specs* (class duration, max capacity, setup time, equipment needed). Members see *benefit language* (not "small group PT" but "personalized attention, results in 8 weeks"). Different brains, different content.

• **Price by value extracted, not time spent.** If your 1:1 coaching gets someone results competitors can't, charge accordingly—don't undercut yourself. Look at what comparable gyms charge in Belfast, then deliberately position higher or lower based on your actual differentiation.

• **Make it scannable in 60 seconds.** A member should understand: class schedule, price, what body part/goal it targets, and how to book. Use a grid or simple visual. If someone has to read paragraphs, it won't be used by your coaches either.

• **Assign one person (probably you) to own version control.** Every price change, new service, or detail update goes through ONE person. Coaches get the same playbook; members see the same offer. Nothing kills trust like conflicting information.

What's your biggest bottleneck right now—do you have too many undefined services, or too few?
